messages:
mina: Hi team — I'm landing a short docs PR to add `stabilization_window_seconds` examples and a note about model-fallback behavior during cross-region failover. Pls quick-eyeball the YAML + Node snippet and the SLA sentence.

tyler: Nice. Quick callout: stabilization windows are additive with cooldowns in the controller; recommend an example where `stabilization_window_seconds` >= `cooldown_seconds` for bursty workloads.

nora: Can you paste the minimal YAML you'll include? I'll convert to a TypeScript SDK example and a one-line CLI.

mina: Draft YAML for the "Stabilization & rollout" subsection:
```yaml
scalepolicy:
  min_replicas: 1
  max_replicas: 15
  metric: rps
  target: 300
  cooldown_seconds: 60
  stabilization_window_seconds: 120
  preemption_policy: relaxed
  fallback_model_policy: regional-fallback
```

nora: TypeScript SDK snippet (short, docs-friendly):
```ts
import { DedicatedClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const c = new DedicatedClient();
await c.applyScalepolicy('tenant-foo', {
  min_replicas: 1,
  max_replicas: 15,
  metric: 'rps',
  target: 300,
  cooldown_seconds: 60,
  stabilization_window_seconds: 120,
  preemption_policy: 'relaxed',
  fallback_model_policy: 'regional-fallback',
});
```

tyler: small nit: mention units (seconds) inline. Also add a short CLI example: `redwoodctl scalepolicy apply --tenant tenant-foo --min 1 --max 15 --metric rps --target 300 --cooldown 60 --stabilization 120 --preemption relaxed --fallback regional-fallback`

mina: Draft SLA blurb I propose to add under "SLA & isolation":
"Fallback model policies and cross-region routing are operational controls that affect where traffic is served during capacity events. Reserved-pool uptime SLAs apply to the availability of the pool; use fallback policies to maintain low-latency serving during outages, but note that routing to fallback model variants can change performance and cost characteristics. For strict locality and performance guarantees, coordinate dedicated capacity and locality commitments with Support."

nora: LGTM but suggest replacing "change performance and cost characteristics" -> "may affect latency and unit cost" (more concrete).

mina: Good edit, will update. Also adding a small migration note: "Legacy fields: `stabilization_ms` -> `stabilization_window_seconds` (divide by 1000). `fallback_policy` -> `fallback_model_policy` with options `regional-fallback|global-fallback|none`."

tyler: QA ask: can someone run a short sim with stabilization_window_seconds=120 and cooldown_seconds=60 to verify we don't see oscillation on synthetic sinusoidal load? I'll run an infra sim tomorrow if no one else can.

qa: I can schedule the sim today in the afternoon, will paste results in this thread. Also will validate that `regional-fallback` routing uses the expected model variant tag.

mina: Thanks — I'll push the PR with the updated wording + snippets. doc-bot, please create preview.

doc-bot: docs-preview created for PR #2719  https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-2719 (lint OK)

qa: SIM NOTES: ran a 30min sinusoidal traffic sim (period 6min). With stabilization_window_seconds=120 we saw reduced replica oscillation vs no stabilization. Peak replica overshoot reduced by ~35%. Routing to regional-fallback triggered in 2 simulated zone outages and latency increased ~12ms on average for fallback requests.

tyler: great numbers, add a short sentence summarizing the sim results under the example.

mina: Added sim summary and updated phrasing. Merging after preview check. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: staging preview build passed for PR #2719  https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-2719

doc-bot: docs build passed for PR #2719 -> main at 2026-03-29T15:22:11Z

mina: Merged and added a short note to the onboarding checklist about stabilization_window_seconds. Closing thread.
